key_points.text: Edit pg_hba.conf to set authentication to trust, such as adding the line 'local all all trust'.
Restart the PostgreSQL server using 'sudo /etc/init.d/postgresql restart'.
Connect as the superuser (e.g., 'psql -U postgres') and run 'ALTER USER my_user_name with password 'my_secure_password';' to reset the password.
Restore the original pg_hba.conf backup and restart the server to re-enable secure authentication.
The error occurs because the primary vacuums old row versions, forcing the standby to cancel queries that need them.
Start a repeatable read transaction on the primary that runs a dummy query and sits idle to prevent vacuuming of old row versions.
Longer queries on the standby will be canceled more often.
The OOMKilled reason and Exit Code 137 indicate the container was terminated because it tried to use more memory than its limit.
Check the application code for a memory leak.
If the application is behaving as expected, consider setting a higher memory limit (and possibly request) for that container.
Add more nodes to the cluster.
Terminate unneeded Pods to make room for pending Pods.
Check that the Pod is not larger than all the nodes, for example a Pod with a request of `cpu: 1.1` will never be scheduled if all nodes have a capacity of `cpu: 1`.
Check for node taints, as the scheduler only considers placements onto nodes that do not have a taint the Pod does not tolerate.
The issue is that the `kubeconfig` is not right.
Run `gcloud container clusters get-credentials "CLUSTER NAME"` to auto-generate it.
Add the missing jackson-databind and jackson-core dependencies to the Java producer.
The crash is caused by the default Linux vm.max_map_count value (around 65535) being exceeded because each log segment consumes 2 map areas.
Creating 50000 partitions results in the allocation of 100000 map areas, which likely causes the broker crash with OutOfMemoryError (Map failed).
The number of log segments per partition varies depending on segment size, load intensity, and retention policy, and generally tends to be more than one.
Compare `pg_current_wal_lsn` on the primary with the `sent_lsn` field in the `pg_stat_replication` view to identify if the primary server is under heavy load.
Compare the `sent_lsn` field from `pg_stat_replication` with `pg_last_wal_receive_lsn` on the standby to identify network delay or heavy load on the standby.
On a hot standby, compare `pg_last_wal_replay_lsn` with the `flushed_lsn` field in the `pg_stat_wal_receiver` view to determine if WAL is being received faster than it can be replayed.
Standard `VACUUM` operations do not return disk space to the operating system, so tables may appear to grow in size even after deleting rows.
To shrink a table back to its minimum size and return the disk space to the operating system, you must use `VACUUM FULL`.
The autovacuum daemon never issues `VACUUM FULL` and aims to maintain steady-state usage rather than minimum table size.
Plain `VACUUM` may not be satisfactory for reclaiming excess disk space in tables with large numbers of dead row versions from massive update or delete activity.
Run `ANALYZE` (or `VACUUM ANALYZE`) on the table to update planner statistics after bulk loading large amounts of data.
Without up-to-date statistics, the planner might make poor decisions during query planning, leading to poor performance.
The Pod is stuck in the `Terminating` state because a deletion was issued, but the control plane is unable to delete the Pod object.
This typically happens if the Pod has a finalizer and an admission webhook prevents the control plane from removing the finalizer.
Check if the cluster has any `ValidatingWebhookConfiguration` or `MutatingWebhookConfiguration` that target `UPDATE` operations for `pods` resources.
The kubelet makes eviction decisions by comparing eviction signals to eviction thresholds, which are the minimum amount of the resource that should be available on the node.
The kubelet uses specific eviction signals including `memory.available`, `nodefs.available`, `imagefs.available`, and `containerfs.available` to monitor resource states.
Each eviction signal supports either a percentage or a literal value, with the percentage calculated relative to the total capacity associated with the signal.
On Linux nodes, the value for `memory.available` is derived from the cgroupfs instead of tools like `free -m`.
Check if you are using a Virtual Private Network (VPN) to access the cluster and ensure the connection is active and stable.
Reconnect to the VPN and try accessing the cluster again if disconnections are suspected.
Increase `max.poll.interval.ms` to allow more time for processing a large batch of records.
Decrease `max.poll.records` to take fewer records so there is enough time to process them.
Explore performance issues within the `poll` loop before changing configuration to avoid masking a bigger problem.
The `.github` folder must be on the branch where the workflow is intended to run.
The `.github` folder must also be on any other branch you want to trigger the workflow from.
Java 17, Java 21, and Java 25 are fully supported.
Java 11 is supported for a subset of modules (clients, streams and related).
Support for versions newer than the most recent LTS version are best-effort.
The `kafka-streams-scala` library is deprecated as of Kafka 4.3.
The `kafka-streams-scala` library will be removed in Kafka 5.0.
Use `node20` for Node.js v20.
Use `node24` for Node.js v24.
Support for MD5-encrypted passwords is deprecated and will be removed in a future release of PostgreSQL.
The MD5 hash algorithm is nowadays no longer considered secure against determined attacks.
If md5 is specified in pg_hba.conf but the user's password is encrypted for SCRAM, SCRAM-based authentication will automatically be chosen instead.
Kafka 0.x clients are not compatible with Kafka 4.0 because pre-0.10.x protocols are fully removed in Kafka 4.0 (KIP-896).
The in-tree Ceph RBD StorageClass provisioner is deprecated in Kubernetes v1.28.
Use a PersistentVolume (PV) and PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) to provide storage with a lifecycle independent of any individual Pod.
PostgreSQL maintains a write ahead log (WAL) in the pg_wal/ subdirectory of the cluster's data directory.
Combine a file-system-level backup with backup of the WAL files to support point-in-time recovery.
pg_dump and pg_dumpall do not produce file-system-level backups and cannot be used as part of a continuous-archiving strategy.
Check the Pod status using `kubectl describe pod` to confirm the termination reason is `OOMKilled`.
Consider setting a higher memory limit (and possibly request) for the container if the application behavior is expected.
Check the application code for a memory leak before increasing limits.
Set the "plugin.name" property to "pgoutput" in the Debezium connector properties.
PostgreSQL provides "pgoutput" and "test_decoding" as the two logical output plugins included in the standard distribution.
Set the resource quota for ephemeral-storage in the namespace.
Specify limits for the ephemeral-storage resource in the Pod spec.
If the user doesn't specify the ephemeral-storage resource limit in the Pod spec, the resource quota is not enforced on ephemeral-storage.
For production clusters with multiple users directly accessing the Kubernetes API, it is recommended to use external authentication sources such as OIDC.
The internal authentication mechanisms, such as client certificates and service account tokens, are not suitable for this use case.
